subject.title: Regression: exec intermittently unavailable in isolated cron sessions (was fixed in 2026.4.1)

question: Should cron `toolsAllow: ["*"]` override restrictive static/provider tool profiles for shell-tool exposure, and should this umbrella be split before any linked PR auto-closes it?
rationale: The open fix path changes scheduled `exec` exposure policy and currently uses a closing reference for an issue that also includes unresolved routing and status-classification modes.

options.title: Accept Cron Wildcard Precedence And Split
options.body: Approve the cron-only wildcard override after security review, but remove or narrow the closing reference so routing/status leftovers stay tracked.

options.title: Keep Profiles Authoritative
options.body: Reject the wildcard override and pursue a fail-closed required-tool/status design that does not widen restrictive profile caps.

options.title: Pause Until One Canonical Design
options.body: Pause the open PRs until maintainers choose a single policy for wildcard, finite allowlists, Codex-native tools, and cron status outcomes.

recommendation.title: Accept Cron Wildcard Precedence And Split
recommendation.body: Approve the cron-only wildcard override after security review, but remove or narrow the closing reference so routing/status leftovers stay tracked.

likelyOwner.reason: The central cron runner split and policy-sensitive owner boundary trace to this history, making this the strongest available routing candidate for the security/product choice.
